problem:
Find the Cartesian equation of the osculating plane for a curve $r(t)$ at the point $P(0,1,3)$ where $t=0,$ given that

$$
T(0)=i,\,N(0)=j.
$$

Note that $T$ and $N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.

feedback.problem:
Find a Cartesian equation of the osculating plane for the curve $r(t)$ at the point where $t=0$, given that

$$
r(t)=⟨-2t,\,{t}^{2},\,-{t}^{2}⟩,\,T(0)=⟨-1,\,0,\,0⟩,\,N(0)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨0,\,1,\,-1⟩
$$

where $T$ and $N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.
feedback.worked_solution:
The position vector of the point where $t=0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}p=r(0) & =⟨-2(0),\,{0}^{2},\,{0}^{2}⟩=⟨0,\,0,\,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to find a vector that's perpendicular to the osculating plane. To do that, we use the cross product of the unit tangent $T(0)$ and the principal normal $N(0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(0)\times N(0) & =⟨-1,\,0,\,0⟩\times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨0,\,1,\,-1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(\left|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,k) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨0,\,-1,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Since we are interested only in the direction of the above vector, let's write our perpendicular vector $n$ as 

$$
n=-\sqrt{2}\cdot (T(0)\times N(0))=⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩.
$$

Finally, let $⟨x,y,z⟩$ denote the position vector of a point on the osculating plane. Since the plane is perpendicular to $n$ and passes through the tip of the position vector $p$, its Cartesian equation can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}(⟨x,y,z⟩-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ ⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot n-p\cdot n & =0 \\ ⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ ⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩ & =⟨0,0,0⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩ \\ 0\cdot x+1\cdot y+1\cdot z & =0 \\ y+z & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
